# AMEVA-Forge Full Technical Specification (v1.0.0)
Official Documentation & Deep Architecture Reference for Autonomous AI Agents.

## 1. System Overview
Browser-Native WebGPU Autograd Deep Learning Engine & Real-Time Interactive Studio
Executes PyTorch-compatible dynamic tensor computations via raw WebGPU WGSL compute shaders with deterministic weakref buffer pooling and zero memory leaks.

## 2. Package & Installation
- PyPI: ameva
- Command: pip install ameva
- Repository: https://github.com/uno-km/AMEVA-Forge

## 3. Core Capabilities
- **Pure WebGPU WGSL Compute Shaders**: Direct GPU hardware dispatching for forward and backward passes with zero JS overhead.
- **PyTorch Syntax Compatibility**: Supports familiar Tensor API, autograd DAG, backward(), and standard optimizers.
- **Leak-Free GPU Buffer Pooling**: Weakref lifecycle management preventing VRAM exhaustion during long training runs.

## 4. Canonical Implementation
```python
import ameva as am

# 1. Initialize WebGPU tensor computation
device = am.device("webgpu" if am.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
x = am.randn(64, 128, device=device, requires_grad=True)
w = am.randn(128, 10, device=device, requires_grad=True)

# 2. Forward pass and backpropagation
y = am.matmul(x, w).relu().sum()
y.backward()
print("Gradients computed on WebGPU:", w.grad.shape)

```
